label: Intelligible species as the form by which an intellect understands
term: intelligible species in ST I q.14 aa.2 and 4
definition: An intelligible species is the form by which the intellect actually understands its object. In human understanding it is a likeness of the object that actualizes the possible intellect, with intelligible being in the knower distinct from the form’s constitutive role in the external thing. In divine self-understanding the divine essence itself is the intelligible species, identical with the intellect and the object understood.
